title: Morphological polarity of the cell is the outward sign of a dynamical polarity

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Morphological polarity of the cell is the outward sign of a dynamical polarity

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: The visible polarity of a cell (symmetry of structure about an axis, such as nucleus–centrosome or free–attached surface) is the outward expression of a real polarised distribution of forces, whose lines of force are made visible where particles of matter become strung together under those forces.

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. IV: On the Internal Form and Structure of the Cell

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: The _morphological_ “polarity” is accompanied by, and is but the outward expression (or part of it) of a true _dynamical_ polarity, or distribution of forces; and the “lines of force” are rendered visible by concatenation of particles of matter, such as come under the influence of the forces in action.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci On Growth and Form claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: D’Arcy Wentworth Thompson, On Growth and Form (1st ed., Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1917), Chapter IV, “On the Internal Form and Structure of the Cell”; topic “Polarity of the resting cell”. Scope: cells with recognisable axes of symmetry, e.g. ova, columnar and ciliated epithelial cells

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on thompson1917-ch04-04: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.52

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: A modern mechanobiological interpretation yields testable correlations and perturbation predictions. Because the historical 'field' is underspecified and many datasets visualize structure rather than force, only restricted versions are resolvable.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Quantify cell-axis morphology and spatial distributions of forces or tension reporters, then test whether morphological polarity predicts a corresponding polarized mechanical field across ova and epithelia. A frequent axis without force anisotropy would refute a strong reading.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Matched force reporters are limited to selected systems.

Visible filament alignment is not an independent force measurement.

'Distribution of forces' has several modern interpretations.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
operationalizability: 0.5
discriminating power: 0.4
data adequacy: 0.45
analysis feasibility: 0.55
data existence: 0.65

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Morphological axes are easy to score, but the claim does not add a measurement that would be true of a force field and false of other polarity mechanisms. Particle chains are both the phenomenon and the supposed proof. The statement therefore has no discriminating empirical consequence.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: The claim identifies visible cell polarity with a polarised force distribution whose lines are the aligned particles. Molecular polarity, cytoskeletal tracks and a physical force field all satisfy that description, so no outcome separates the claim from its rivals.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Aligned organelles are the observation the wording treats as the evidence of the forces.

Any successful polarity mechanism can be redescribed as dynamical polarity.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
operationalizability: 0.2
data adequacy: 0.2
analysis feasibility: 0.25
discriminating power: 0.15
data existence: 0.3
